callout.text: The field stops us from drowning

storyboard.claim: The field rejects almost everything so society does not drown in novelty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield: the field as protection against chaos, with the gatekeeper pointing away the flood of new work.
storyboard.onScreenText: The field stops us from drowning
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the earlier point that the field must reject most new work.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the rejection a purpose: it keeps people afloat.

storyboard.claim: A person proposes an idea and the field disposes of it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A young man holds up his notes while a door icon marks the exit the field closes on him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the field rejecting almost everything.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts a person on the proposing side so the viewer sees who gets turned away.

storyboard.claim: Gatekeepers decide whether an idea gets to exist in the wider culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The grey-suited gatekeeper beside the door icon: access to culture is controlled.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the earlier general point to the gatekeepers themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door shows exclusion, not a private basement idea being shown.

callout.text: When and where you are born

storyboard.claim: If gatekeepers hold the keys, birth time and place must matter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A key: whoever holds the keys decides who gets in, so the time and place of birth decide access.
storyboard.onScreenText: When and where you are born
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the gatekeeper point into the question of context.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the two variables, birth time and place, that the narrator then tests.

storyboard.claim: Perfect timing is a myth; environmental convergence is the reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the struck phrase carries the rejection.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the question about context with a verdict.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the myth so the viewer hears the rejection, not an endorsement of timing luck.

storyboard.claim: Florence in 1401: a room of anxious, wealthy merchants.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An intact city icon for Florence; a worried, sharp older figure stands in for the wealthy merchants in the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the historical scene that the systems argument rests on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Dates and places the scene so the viewer knows when and where.

storyboard.claim: The guild is obsessing over the details of a bronze door mockup.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worried gatekeeper thinking over a panel of detail; the door is named by the callout, not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the room of merchants to the commission they are judging.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what the commission is: a bronze door.

storyboard.claim: A 21-year-old is handed a huge commission and paid handsomely.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A nervous young man in a blue tunic holding a coin: the wages he is being paid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the person the commission lands on.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the name, spelled correctly, and ties the pay to a physical coin.

storyboard.claim: The merchants hover over the young man, judging every strike.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The angry gatekeeper pointing at the young apprentice at his bench: she is pressing him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the pressure from the previous beat onto the body of the apprentice.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the judging as a confrontation, not a passive audience.

storyboard.claim: The merchants demand absolute perfection from the kid.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An angry gatekeeper talking at the apprentice: a demand, a threat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the pressure; now the demand is spoken.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the demand in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: Great creative leaps happen when a domain and a field converge.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step chain: domain, then field, then creative leap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the anecdote into the general rule.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the causal order the narrator states as a rule.

storyboard.claim: The convergence acts like a vacuum that pulls talent up to meet demand.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor speaking as the vacuum image in words; the callout carries the metaphor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the vacuum metaphor just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what the vacuum pulls: talent.

storyboard.claim: The Renaissance was not a genetic burst or something in the water.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the struck phrase is the rejected explanation.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the biological explanation before the next claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the folk explanation so it is not endorsed.

storyboard.claim: You do not need a lone genius in an empty room; you need an environment that funds, demands and scrutinizes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing away from the empty room: the rejected figure is named by the struck phrase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the rejection of the individual-only myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the phrase the narrator rejects, so no lone genius is shown.

storyboard.claim: A spark, meaning a new idea, needs an environment to burn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A lightbulb: the spark of an idea, with the callout giving the oxygen metaphor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Bridges from the rejection to the example about to follow.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what the spark needs: oxygen, meaning environment.

storyboard.claim: Architecture was expanding because Roman ruins were being rediscovered and studied.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor holding a book, thinking over the study of old buildings.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the first domain factor, architecture's knowledge base.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the knowledge came from studying ruins, using a book as the source.

storyboard.claim: Ancient math came back online while bankers gained wealth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing at the callout: the ancient knowledge is named.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second strand of the collision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the knowledge returning as the math of antiquity.

storyboard.claim: The bankers were rich but anxious and needed to show off.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon for status; a smirking merchant figure for display and vanity.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the money side of the collision.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the wealth is used as status, not as a neutral fact.

callout.text: The past collided with the present

storyboard.claim: Rival city-states drove a collision of past knowledge and present money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A city icon for the rival city-states; the callout names the collision.
storyboard.onScreenText: The past collided with the present
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the historical collision from the previous beats.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the rivalry as the reason the legacy was wanted.

storyboard.claim: The host is struggling with what the systems view implies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried host thinking: the confusion is shown in the face and posture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the challenge to the environmental argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the next beat as a question from the audience's side.

storyboard.claim: If the environment dictates everything, were the artists not geniuses?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking the challenge; the callout states the premise under test.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the historical argument into the implication being questioned.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the premise being questioned in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: No: the host is not saying the artists were not geniuses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the struck phrase is the rejected reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the challenge with a denial.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the reading the narrator rejects, so it is not endorsed.

storyboard.claim: Not just anyone could cast those doors: it takes rare skill, dedication and vision.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor, admired and rare: a single figure who stands out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts with the claim that anyone could have done it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says how rare the required talent is.

storyboard.claim: The systems view is humbling: the individual is not the sole source.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the callout marks the turn in the argument.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pivots from the rare-talent point to the systems view.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames what comes next as the humbling part of the argument.

storyboard.claim: Had the apprentice died as a child, someone else would have built the doors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A grave icon as the death the sentence imagines; the apprentice looks sad, never happy over death.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the thought experiment that tests the systems argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Marks the hypothetical so the viewer does not take it as a fact.

storyboard.claim: Someone else would have built the doors, shaped slightly differently.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host pointing at the callout: another builder is named as the replacement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the thought experiment with its result.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the conclusion of the experiment in the narrator's words.

storyboard.claim: The domain gives the tools, the field gives the cash and demand, and the person pours talent into the mold.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-step chain: domain tools, field cash, then the person's talent.
storyboard.onScreenText: Domain tools -> Field cash -> Person's talent
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Summarises the mold idea as a chain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows which part each system supplies and which part the person adds.

storyboard.claim: What makes a specific person survive the pressure?
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried host thinking over the question of survival under pressure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Asks the next question after the mold metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the question the next beats answer.

storyboard.claim: Talent versus drive is the question the study answers, and the data is surprising.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the callout sets the two terms against each other.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the survival question with the two candidates.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the two variables the data compares.

storyboard.claim: A 12-year-old boy named John Wheeler is the example that breaks the prodigy myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy scientist at a library corner, absorbed and thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the example for the talent-versus-drive question.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the age so the viewer sees he is a child, not a prodigy on show.

storyboard.claim: A normal 12-year-old might read a comic or play outside; he is hanging out in a library.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy seated in the library with a book, the ordinary kid's activity shown as the contrast.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes his setting while his father is away.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts him with the normal 12-year-old the narrator mentions.

storyboard.claim: He is whittling wooden gears to build a primitive calculating machine.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boy at a workbench, focused on the gears he carves.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows what he is doing in the library.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says what he makes: wooden gears for a machine.

storyboard.claim: He does not care about grades, sports or normal kid stuff; he wants to know how gears click.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A blank-faced boy turned away from the classroom, showing indifference to school.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes his indifference to school.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the indifference through the blank face instead of drawing the negated grades.

storyboard.claim: He grows up to be one of the most prominent theoretical physicists of the 20th century.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon for the status he reaches; the boy celebrates the outcome.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the Wheeler example.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the outcome of the obsession shown in the library.

storyboard.claim: World-changing creativity is rarely born in flawless childhood prodigies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the struck phrase is the rejected figure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises from the Wheeler example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the prodigy image so it is not endorsed.

storyboard.claim: The myth is the genius who looks at a chalkboard and solves the universe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor pointing at the classroom chalkboard; the struck phrase is the myth.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the cultural myth the previous beat rejected.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the myth so the viewer hears it as a myth.

storyboard.claim: You do not need a 170 IQ to change a domain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking; the struck figure is the rejected requirement.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Answers the effortless-genius myth with the data.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the IQ requirement so the viewer does not take it as needed.

storyboard.claim: What you need is an intense curiosity that keeps attention focused for decades.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A fire icon for intense, burning curiosity; the boy thinking over his work.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Says what replaces the IQ requirement.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the time dimension: decades of focus.

storyboard.claim: Rosalyn Yalow, a Nobel laureate, was open that a classmate was naturally smarter than her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The host speaking about the named example; the callout gives the correctly spelled name.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the real example of drive over raw talent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the correct spelling of the name the transcript garbled.

storyboard.claim: Physical chemistry is an incredibly brutal subject that the classmates took together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A worried, slumped student: the subject is shown as a grind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the classmate story that the next beat continues.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the subject as brutal, which is what makes the effort matter.
